original_question: If (X, d) is a non-separable metric space, must its Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) contain a closed copy of the space omega_1 x (omega_1 + 1)?
target_in_paper: Question 2.8 in Section 2 ("The Normality Problem and Associated Questions"): for a non-separable metric space (X,d), must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) contain a closed copy of ω1 × (ω1 + 1)? This is asked immediately after Proposition 2.6 and Theorem 2.7 as the sharper embedding question relevant to the normality problem. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it has the right hypothesis ((X,d) non-separable metric), the right hyperspace ((2^X, T_W(d))), and the right target space (ω1 × (ω1 + 1)) as a closed copy. In substance, it matches Question 2.8 almost verbatim. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
missing_details: The paper fixes 2^X to mean the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, not the full power set. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

To be fully stand-alone, T_W(d) should be identified as the Wijsman topology induced by d; equivalently, it is the weakest topology on 2^X making every map A ↦ d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a): a∈A} continuous for x∈X. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

"Closed copy" should be spelled out as a closed subspace homeomorphic to ω1 × (ω1 + 1). ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

The ordinal spaces ω1 and ω1 + 1 are taken with their usual order topologies, and the product uses the product topology. This is standard but implicit in the paper’s wording. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

The nearby context matters: Proposition 2.6 proves the existence of such a closed copy only inside the punctured subspace 2^X\{X}, while Question 2.8 asks whether one can strengthen this to the whole Wijsman hyperspace. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
refined_question: Let (X,d) be a non-separable metric space, let 2^X denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X induced by d (equivalently, the weakest topology making each map A ↦ d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a): a∈A}, x∈X, continuous). Must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) contain a closed subspace homeomorphic to ω1 × (ω1 + 1), where ω1 and ω1 + 1 carry their usual order topologies? ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. In Section 2, Proposition 2.6 shows that for every non-separable metric space (X,d), the subspace 2^X\{X} contains a closed copy of ω1 × (ω1 + 1). Theorem 2.7 then derives consequences for metrizability and hereditary normality. The paper immediately asks whether Proposition 2.6 can be improved from the punctured hyperspace to the full hyperspace, and that exact question is labeled Question 2.8. So your draft should be sharpened only by unpacking notation and topology conventions, not broadened to the neighboring Question 2.9 about arbitrary non-normal Wijsman hyperspaces. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
